Mrs. Jnd Mathison, who taught private classes in piano for College students for the first three years of the school's life, was the granddaughter of John Sevier, the first governor of the "State of Franklin" (later Tennessee), United States Senator, and famous as a Revolutionary hero. She was born December 21, 1840, in Henry County, Tennessee, the daughter of James A. and Sabra (Elliston) Yowell, and reared and educated in Tennessee. She married E. J. Mathison, a Northern educator and philanthropist, and left Texas in 1870. Her work as a teacher in Savoy was closely connected with the college, since most of her piano pupils were drawn from the school. Her son-in-law, Mr. George Lindsay, of Houston, recalls the spell-binding thrill of the programs given by Professor Holland's students at the College, and the musical background and accompaniment which Mrs. Mathison provided. When the Mathisons moved from Savoy they went first to Whitewright and then to Nashville, Tennessee, and then to different places on their ler and Susie. Some years later they came back to Texas and settled in Greenville, where Mrs. Mathison died October 18, 1926.

Miss Kate Hunderhult, who was advertised in the Philomean Messenger as being head of the Music Department of the College during approximately 1883-86, was a graduate of Ward's Seminary at Nashville.

Miss Frankie Chesworth, one of the later teachers of music, was the daughter of George F. and Mary E. (Patty) Chesworth. She was born July 1, 1871, and graduated from Savoy College in 1888 with a diploma in Music and the A. B. degree. She then returned to teach in the College. Her
